name: Frontline plc

vlcc.note: MEG weight solved from reported TCE: 10% in 2026Q2, 15% in 2026Q3. 12% adopted. !! REGIME-DEPENDENT, NOT A CONSTANT. 12% is a Hormuz-disrupted weight. A large part of the VLCC fleet is committed to Arabian Gulf trades - idle inside the Gulf, shuttling across the strait, or loading at Fujairah and along the Omani coast (Frontline Q2 2026 tanker market update) - which pushes Frontline's exposure toward the Atlantic and so toward TD15/TD22. If Hormuz normalises the MEG share rises and this weight has to be re-solved from the next reported TCE. Do not treat it as settled.

smax.note: Mean of the routes PRESENT in the week. A blank route is excluded from the average, never counted as zero. That is deliberate, but it means the basket changes over time and the series is not one consistent definition: of 236 weeks only 11 carry all three, 133 are TD20 alone and 99 are TD20+TD27. TD33 first appears 2026-08-07, so every back-test quarter through 2026Q2 was fitted without it. Measured on the 11 weeks where all three exist, TD20 alone runs -0.21% mean and 1.99% mean absolute against the full basket, worst case +5.5% - small, but n=11 and all from one regime. Backfilling TD27 and TD33 from the archived weeklies is the real fix.

blend.note_ballast_regime: BALLAST, and why it needs no adjustment. Ballast enters the model three times and none of them is a variable. (1) Inside the Baltic blend: the route TCEs are round-voyage, net of the ballast leg, so a more ballast-heavy voyage prints a lower rate on its own. (2) Inside the realised_uplift: that ratio is Frontline's realised TCE - total spot earnings over total spot days, ballast days in the denominator - divided by our blend, so any ballast they carry BEYOND a standard voyage lands there. (3) Inside coverage.k: uncovered days earn a quarter of the contracted rate precisely because they are mostly ballast. CORRECTION 2026-11-04: an earlier version of this note said Atlantic voyages carry a higher ballast share than MEG. That is wrong per unit of TIME, which is what fills a quarter. MEG is the highest at 46.7% (45d round voyage, 24d load-to-discharge), against Brazil/China 38.2% and USG/Far East 20.9% - the longer the laden leg, the smaller the ballast return as a fraction. The frequency effect cancels exactly: more voyages x fewer ballast days each is the same share of time. So a Hormuz-driven skew toward the Atlantic LOWERS structural ballast, from 31.6% at a 12% MEG weight toward 29.5% at zero. Disclosed ballast nonetheless rose 19.2% (2025Q4) to 26.3% (2026Q2), so route mix is swamped by repositioning and waiting - ballast attached to no fixture, which route arithmetic cannot see. Measured effect on the uplift: regressing it on ballast share over the 8 post-Euronav quarters gives uplift = 1.103 - 0.333 x ballast, R2 0.08, residual sd 0.043. Across the whole observed range of 19-32% the uplift moves 4% and Q4 2026 moves 447k to 431k. The residual scatter is about twice the size of the effect, and the calibration mean is already 24.9% ballast, so the disrupted regime is most of the sample rather than outside it. No adjustment applied: it would be fitting noise, and the 3.2x rate extrapolation is the risk that matters.

realised_uplift.note: Benchmark blend -> Frontline-realised TCE. Applied at SERIES CONSTRUCTION, to observed weeks only, never inside the kernel and never to a forecast anchor the user types - that is already owner-level, and marking it up again was the 140 -> 147 bug. VLCC 1.02 is MEASURED: realised VLCC TCE / our blend over the 8 post-Euronav quarters (2024Q3-2026Q2) is mean 1.020, sd 0.044. It is 1.020 at a blend of 101,437 (2026Q1) and 1.018 at 150,097 (2026Q2), and corr(rate level, ratio) = +0.02 - capture does not fade as rates rise, over the range we can see. Was 1.05, fitted across 2022-2026, a period spanning two different fleets. SMAX 1.03 is NOT measured on the same basis: the Suezmax basket is not one consistent series (of 236 weeks only 11 carry all three routes), so the ratio cannot be computed cleanly. It is carried forward unchanged and is the weakest constant in the model.

kernel.note: a is the lag from a fixture being ASSESSED to it starting to earn; b is the load-to-discharge window over which that revenue is recognised. a+b is NOT the round voyage - the next cargo is fixed partway through the current one, so there is no reason they match. Assuming they did is what made the fitted a look wrong for two sessions.
kernel.b_evidence: FITTED, not measured. CORRECTED 2026-11-13: the earlier claim here - that 17 broker fixtures measured b at 66.4d - multiplied the ballast/laden/port percentages by rv_days when they are a share of actual_days. The source carries both and they are different voyages (rv - actual runs -7 to +45 days against idle under 1.5d). On the correct base the same fixtures give Brazil/China 49.9d, USG/Far East 70.0d, blended 56.3d - 15% below the 66 in use. MEG/East is now MEASURED at 29.9d from 5 routed Frontline fixtures, not assumed at 24.0d. See data/voyage_cycle.md. b therefore has no independent support and stands on its curve fit. Q4 2026 is insensitive at 88% fed: b=66 gives 491,905 and b=56 gives 517,621, so the value in use is the conservative one.
kernel.a_evidence: FITTED, not measured. 14 days is the lag from Baltic assessment to commencement of loading - roughly a laycan lead. The fixture data carries open dates but not laycan, so this is the one VLCC parameter with no direct measurement. At b=66 the fit is flat between a=10 and a=18.
kernel.smax_caveat: Suezmax 20/44 is scaled, not measured - no Suezmax voyage splits yet, and its route basket is not a consistent series (see blend.smax.note). The weakest parameters in the model.

coverage.note: Share of the CONTRACTED rate that the uncovered days earn, by segment. Measured as earned_uncovered / uncovered_days / contracted_rate over 17 quarters of disclosure (data/quarter_fill.csv): VLCC median 0.26 mean 0.28, Suezmax 0.55/0.55, Aframax 0.45/0.45. Was a single 0.27 for all three, which is right for VLCC and roughly half what the data says for Suezmax. The ordering follows voyage length: Suezmax b=44 vs VLCC b=66, so a cargo fixed after the report date still lands more of its load-to-discharge window inside the quarter, and the Suezmax tail is less ballast-heavy. Back-test of coverage() with these values: VLCC mean |err| 3%, Suezmax 5%, Aframax 9%, against 8% with a single 0.27.

required_yields.note: 0.24 is not an assumption. On 28 August 2026, the day the slide was published, FRO closed at $41.40 against the slide's own $10.35 base-case FCF/share - a 25.0% cap rate. 24% sits a point inside that.

nav.note: Needs fleet.csv (vessel, segment, build year) and a broker value curve. Xclusiv VLCC assessments 18 Sep 2026: 5yr $172m, 10yr $152m, 15yr $135m; newbuild ~$131-135m. Early July for comparison: $145m / $115m / $83.5m. The age curve has collapsed - buyers paying for immediate availability. Frontline's Euronav tonnage skews old, so NAV is levered to the end of the curve that moved most.

quarters_note: The window opens on the nearest UNREPORTED quarter and rolls forward one when Frontline reports. That first quarter always has a disclosed coverage % and contracted rate, so it is priced with coverage() and is frozen - the forward-curve controls cannot move it. Later quarters have no disclosure and use the kernel.

consensus.source: Normalized EPS, retrieved 2026-11-04. Analyst count is per column: 3 for Q3, 2 for Q4, 4 for FY2026, 5 for FY2027.
consensus.note: Reference only, never an input. The Q4 estimate has not moved since before the spike began: 1.40 / 1.60 / 1.58 / 1.58 / 1.58 at 90/60/30/7/0 days, while the Q3 estimate rose 1.38 -> 2.27 over the same window. Consensus Q4 of 1.58 implies a VLCC spot TCE of about 92,000/day, below Q3 and a seventh of what is already locked in printed weeks.
consensus.basis: Normalized EPS equals Frontline's ADJUSTED profit per share, which is what our bridge produces: ours gives 1.55 (2026Q1) and 2.61 (2026Q2) and the reports state exactly those. Frontline's GAAP figures for the same quarters were 2.51 and 2.96. TradingView's EPS series is GAAP and is NOT comparable - do not substitute it here.

tce_to_profit.note: Total TCE less adjusted profit, calibrated on 2026Q2: TCE 753.3, adjusted profit 580.2. Largely fixed costs, so it is held flat across quarters - a simplification that will understate the gap if the fleet grows. Used only to translate the forecast into EPS for comparison with consensus.
